To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the long run average auditing cost is a function of the number of audit events, the cost per audit event, the number of users and the cost per user, the number of audit periods, the cost per period, and the cost of the database.
the periodic auditing strategy is more cost effective for small values of the parameter and that the counting strategy is more cost efficient for large values of the parameter.

the long run average operating cost for the counting auditing strategy is equal to the long run average of the operating cost of the periodic auditing strategy, and that the long run operating costs of the counting and time dependent strategies are identical.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the long run operating costs of auditing databases.
the long run average operating cost of auditing a database and the effect of various auditing strategies on this cost.
the long run operating costs of running continuous audit.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the periodic auditing strategy is better than the counting strategy.
, in the case where auditing errors are not too frequent, the counting strategy is the best choice, whereas in the case where the errors are frequent, the periodic strategy is the best.
, the periodic auditing strategy is the most cost effective strategy for minimizing the long term operating cost of database audit.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we show that the counting and periodic strategies are not optimal in minimizing the cost of continuous database audit.
the counting strategy dominates the periodic strategy for a wide range of parameter settings.
the counting strategy is better than the periodic strategy when the cost of auditing is high, the cost of error is low and the error probability is low.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the counting strategy has lower long run average cost than the periodic strategy when the cost of auditing a single database transaction is low and the cost of auditing the database is high.
the periodic auditing strategy is not optimal in the long run.
the periodic auditing strategy is not always the best strategy.
